intro: Nocturn (or the office in the middle of the night) is an office that arose from a custom to say the longest psalm during the night. It is customary to say it either after rising from bed in the morning, or to anticipate it in the evening (independently on when Matins is said).
vigil_note: On vigil-ranked feasts such as today, the Typicon’s principal provision is that Great Vespers pass directly into Matins. Nocturn is thus not said, or said as a private prayer after rising from sleep.
troparia_2: (Tone 2) Remember Your servants, O Lord, because of Your goodness,* and forgive all sins they committed in life,* for no one is sinless but You,* Who alone can give rest to the departed.

(Tone 8) With profound wisdom and love for mankind, You arrange all things* and bestow beneficial things upon all, O only Creator and Lord.* Grant rest to the souls of your servants,* for they have placed their hope in You,* our God Who made and shaped us.
(Tone 8, kontakion) With the Saints grant rest, O Christ,* to the souls of Your servants,* where there is neither pain, nor sorrow, nor sighing,* but life everlasting.

O Virgin Godbearer, we, all generations, bless you.* For in you the uncontainable Christ our God was pleased to be contained.* We are blessed in having you as our advocate.* You intercede for us day and night.* Rulers are made strong by your intercession.* And so we shout out and sing your praises:* Hail, O Woman Full of Grace, the Lord is with you!
prayer_dead: Lord, remember our fathers and brothers who have fallen asleep in the hope of resurrection to eternal life and all who have died in piety and faith. Forgive every sin, voluntary and involuntary, committed by them in word or deed or thought. Give them rest in a place of light, in a place of refreshment, in a place of repose from which has fled all pain, sorrow and sighing, where the light of Your countenance shines and gladdens Your saints from of old. Grant them Your kingdom and a share in Your ineffable and eternal good things and the enjoyment of Your everlasting, blessed life. For You are the Life, the Resurrection and Repose of Your servants who have fallen asleep, O Christ our God, and we give glory to You together with Your eternal Father and Your all-holy, good, and life-giving Spirit, now and for ever and ever. Amen.
prayer_dead_omitted: Prayer for the departed is omitted today.
